distinguishing_features: Passive hardware design change (thermal spreader insert + PCB layout modification) that reduces the joint's local ΔT, rather than a software inference/monitoring scheme or a procedural duty-cycle setpoint change.
Applies the mitigation to the electrical/thermal path of an electronic assembly (solder joint CTE-mismatch strain) rather than to turbine liners/blades or reactor-wall fouling.
Reduces joint ΔT by spreading heat flux away from the joint before it arrives, instead of derating combustion temperature or thermally shocking a fouling layer.
No prior art shares the load path, hardware class, or failure-physics coupling (Δα·ΔT at the solder joint).
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce the cyclic thermal strain amplitude at a solder joint driven by CTE mismatch under power cycling, so as to extend fatigue life.
parsed.viable_reason: Adding a high-conductivity spreader to lower the local joint ΔT is a physically sound, passive, standard-materials design that is directly testable per the stated protocol.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The prior art references are all unrelated monitoring/derating/fouling schemes, so reducing joint ΔT via a spreader outside the joint thermal path is not an obvious application of that art to this problem.
